author: Nancy Stordahl
title: Comments - Lesson plans - when things (& life) don't go as planned
text:
Woah! Nancy ... your words land like a truth-telling bell, ringing with urgency and care. “Plans of hope” ... what a powerful phrase. You’ve named the heartbreak, the improvisation and that fierce love it takes to keep going. Thank you so much for refusing numbness and calling us to act. Your list is clear, doable and deeply needed. I’ll be sharing it and standing with you.
I think the thing that upsets me most is that these school shooting tragedies are now expected. Perhaps it's because I live in the UK, but I struggle to even comprehend this devastating reality. And yet, as you say, we bear it. We numb. We move on. Your refusal to do so is a gift.
Thank you for naming the exhaustion, the absolute terror, the sheer resilience and for ending this post not in despair, but with action. May your words ripple outward. May your grief be witnessed. And may your fierce love for all children continue to guide us toward something better.
In answer to first questions: What unexpected curveball has life thrown you? What helps you change course, adapt, or just keep going? Well, too many to list and how I usually deal with them has me searching for my walking boots and heading out. In fact, walking, helps me no end with everything life has thrown at me ... for as long as I can remember.
And with your third question: Do you have an idea to help keep our kids safer in schools? I’d say one powerful step is fostering cross-cultural dialogue ... sharing what works elsewhere, listening deeply to each other, and standing together in global solidarity for safer schools and braver action. Wow! What a compassionate, helpful post, I'm so pleased you decided to change tracks and go with your heart today. 🙏💖🔔
